passage:
Sonali, you asked why I deleted my "goals" folder. So, I'm Mehak, and for six months I followed all these gym and makeup creators, and every morning I felt I had to change something: my hair, my stomach, my skin. I bought things I didn't need.
Then one night I watched one of them pitch a "transformation plan", her discount code flashing in the same breath as telling us how much we needed fixing. I thought: who earns when I feel inadequate? She does.
So I unfollowed most of them. Now I follow a swimming coach who posts drills and a science teacher who explains how things work. My mornings are quieter. I still notice myself comparing sometimes, but now I ask who is selling what.

qa.q: What flashed on screen with the influencer's transformation plan?
qa.a: Her discount code flashed on screen in the same breath as the plan.

qa.q: What was Mehak feeling every morning while following the influencers?
qa.a: She felt she had to change something, like her hair, stomach or skin, which suggests envy and a sense of not being enough.

qa.q: What did Mehak change about whom she follows, and why?
qa.a: She unfollowed most of them after asking who earns when she feels inadequate, and now picks accounts that teach real things. 😊

qa.q: How might the influencer see her transformation plan?
qa.a: She may see it as a product and her followers as customers, so she benefits when viewers feel they need fixing.

grounding: Shows a teen envying fitness and beauty influencers, asking who benefits from her inadequacy and choosing accounts for evidence and wellbeing.
